content.comment_body: Hello, I am experiencing the same issue. The IP configuration is set up correctly, and I can connect several [product_name] devices on the network. I started by configuring my company's email, which is a Gmail account (SMTP.GMAIL.COM). I tried all three security protocol options and ports 25, 465, and 587. After entering the email and password, it still would not work. With port 25, the status indicator is initially green but turns red due to a timeout. Out of options, I set up a routing on my Gmail Workspace using SMTP-RELAY.GMAIL.COM, but that also failed. This email feature is very important for receiving machine alarms and maintenance signals. It's frustrating how complicated this is, especially compared to tutorial videos that make it look easy. Thank you in advance for any help. [user_name]
Please use English in this forum. For [product_name] IP settings, make sure to set: the IP address, subnet mask, and gateway. Also, ensure time and date settings are correct.

The IP works locally and the clock is correct. Using [version_no] (GB). I have the same issue and followed similar steps as previously described: correct IP setup, using Gmail (SMTP.GMAIL.COM), tried various security options and ports, with no success using my email and password. Routing via SMTP-RELAY.GMAIL.COM also yielded no results. This function is very useful for receiving machine alarms and maintenance notifications. It’s surprisingly complicated despite the ease shown in online tutorials. Thanks for any support. [user_name]
Perhaps this helps: Use Google-managed SSL certificates with Load Balancing on Google Cloud.

I was able to send a test email, although not with Gmail, but via one.com. I have both a website and email account with one.com. My setup: Server name SEND.ONE.COM, Security: STARTTLS, Port: 587, my email and password entered. The test email was sent to my personal Gmail account and worked. The message received stated that the email was generated automatically by [product_name] version [version_no], and included multiple language samples and technical details. I later received an alarm email when my machine had an issue, which shows functionality. I feel disappointed that the product is advertised with unlimited possibilities but cannot work reliably with Gmail, which is widely used. The workaround uses a mail server with potentially less security and reliability. I do not understand why [company_name] released a product with such issues. I hope this alternative solution can help others.
To use Gmail, you must create an app password in your Google account. Then use TLS with port 465. I successfully tested this on [product_name] version [version_no].
Hello, I followed the instructions and created the app password, but it did not work correctly. I attached my screen for reference. Did you add any CA certificate?

Hi everyone, I managed to configure [product_name] version [version_no] to send emails through Gmail. Step 1: Set up Gmail SMTP as shown in the recommended YouTube video. At the end, generate an app password for use in step 2. Step 2: In [product_name] online settings > email settings: set server as smtp.gmail.com, security as STARTTLS, port 587, and use your Gmail login. The password must be the generated 16-digit app password without spaces in the password field.
Thanks, my friend! It’s working now!

Hello all, thanks in advance for your support. I tried all the recommended steps but cannot send emails from [product_name]. Using an SMTP tool, I can send emails, but not from [product_name]. Are there other settings I should check? Regards, [user_name]
Hi, If Gmail is too complicated or restrictive, try switching to a different free email provider. There are many alternatives available.
Yes, these are the correct settings and they worked for me. Thanks, [user_name]
Did you manage to solve the issue? If so, please share your solution. I'm facing the same difficulty.
I am experiencing the same problem.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered persistent problems configuring email functionality with Gmail on [product_name] hardware using recommended options, security protocols, and ports. Some achieved success through alternative email servers like one.com, while Gmail required generating an app-specific password and precise security configurations. The setup process was viewed as overly complex relative to marketing and tutorials, leading to user frustration. Questions arose regarding possible certificate requirements, and several users have not resolved the issue yet.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a simple, dependable email setup using Gmail with [product_name] hardware, as shown in official demonstrations. They expect clear and comprehensive guidance for any additional steps (such as app passwords and certificates) so that the feature works smoothly in typical scenarios.
